method: Independent raw-flux local quadratic baseline plus finite-exposure trapezoids. Separate even/odd shape; unconstrained per-event depths; empirical out-of-event error floor and fit-residual inflation.
caveats: Amplitudes describe unconvolved trapezoid peaks, not physical eclipse depths or radius ratios.
Four-pair blocks only approximate within-sector noise correlations.
Alternating eclipses support a double-period binary but do not locate the eclipsing source or confirm stellar masses.
A planet at the doubled period could show primary/secondary eclipses, but a several-thousand-ppm optical occultation of a Sun-like host would require an exceptionally luminous object.

noiseless_actual_cadence_equal_depth.note: Numerical control of cadence integration and baseline/depth projection at a known fixed shape. Not an injection-recovery completeness measurement or noise false-alarm test.

error_fallback.method: All supplied flux errors are invalid; substituted robust first-difference scatter divided by sqrt(2), then retained local out-of-event floors.

weighted_paired_contrast.note: Inverse-variance weights downweight one poorly constrained sector28 eclipse. Cluster uncertainty permits an independent mean offset in each sector; only five clusters means its tail calibration is unreliable. Error-model choices materially change the quoted sigma.

sensitivity_omitting_one_largest_error_p.note: Diagnostic only: retained in the principal analyses. Selection uses the measurement error rather than its eclipse depth.

paired_contrast.limitations: Conditional fixed-template test. Shape/ephemeris were fit on these data; pairs may share systematics. Bootstrap confidence intervals do not establish Gaussian tail probabilities or survey false-alarm rates.
